evidence.quote: | Ready, Some books when Transfer.holdsRecords books ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: All the new rules live in Tier 2. Summa.Storage.Transfer owns the file format, the order of refusals, the data-version check and the 'already holds records' predicate. The engine (also Tier 2) decides when GitHub books are refused, when the files pack is missing, when import is allowed, and what notice to show. The only Tier 3 change maps three kernel event names to engine messages and decides nothing.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect below Tier 4. The time comes in through ctx.Now. The download is returned as an OfferDownload effect value, and the save goes through the existing `save` path (a SaveBooks effect), so the edge carries both out. Transfer.fs uses only Arca's pure Json/Codec and System.Globalization, with no System.IO or System.Text.Json. The decisions can be tested without effects.

evidence.quote: | _, _, false -> { model with Error = Some "This browser cannot offer downloads here." }, []

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Most facts have one definition: Schema, Version, Exports.Classification, Exports.dataVersion, LocalSnapshot.encode/decode and Transfer.holdsRecords are each defined once and referenced. Two facts are restated as literals, though the copies agree. The exportedAt timestamp format is written twice, once in the writer (stamp) and once in the reader (exportedAtOf). The requirement calls the downloads error an existing message, but the change types it out again instead of referencing it.

evidence.quote: | [], _ when version = 2 && declaredContents file <> Some(contents restored.Books) ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Tier 2 (Summa.Storage.Transfer) defines what the books hold and the contents-mismatch refusal. The preview is projected in the Tier 2 engine by calling Transfer.read and Transfer.contents. Counts come from the books for every file version, not from the declared counts, as F2 requires. Tier 3/4 gain only a data-text binding in index.html.

evidence.quote: | BooksTransferTextChanged v -> { model with BooksTransferText = v; BooksTransferPreview = transferPreview v }, []

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effects. The preview is a pure function of the pasted text and returns no effect, and version-2 writing and reading stay pure in Transfer.fs.

evidence.quote: | Ok version when version <> 1 && version <> 2 -> Error $"Transfer files of version {version} cannot be read here."
| [], _ when version = 2 && declaredContents file <> Some(contents restored.Books) ->

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one authority: Transfer.contents is used by export, by read's check and by the engine preview. But the set of readable versions, and which version carries contents, are written as bare literals 1 and 2 in read, not taken from the Version constant. The copies agree today. If Version is bumped and read is not updated, the module would refuse files it writes itself.
